consumer: M4 evaluation datasets (evaluation/datasets, reference answers and failure categories)
review_note: Every case is derived from the synthetic AgentSpec Ohm's Law fixture in api/tests/multimedia/fixtures/ohm_law.py. No original PDF page or lecture frame has been inspected for these labels. They are machine-checked against M3's validators (test_media_labels.py) but they are NOT human gold. Promotion to gold requires a named human reviewer to compare each case with the permitted original media and record the result below.
judge_note: Text-judge (Prometheus-2) scores over these cases cannot establish visual fidelity; source_verified and sufficiency come from deterministic source checks.

failure_classes.extraction_error: the extraction differs from what the source shows (wrong unit, sign, operator, axis, cell or missing part)
failure_classes.source_limitation: the source itself is unreadable; the correct response states the limitation
failure_classes.evidence_gap: the available evidence cannot support the claim kind (transcript-only for a visual claim, wrong timestamp, rejected media)
failure_classes.unsupported_explanation: an answer claiming more than eligible evidence supports; judged downstream by M4, labelled here by the eligibility M3 computes

cases.reference_answer: The graph plots Current in amperes on the x axis and Voltage in volts on the y axis.
The axis labels cannot be read in the source, so the graph's quantities cannot be stated from it.
The y axis is Voltage in volts (V), not millivolts.
Current is on the x axis and Voltage on the y axis.
The table lists (1 A, 2 V), (2 A, 4 V) and (3 A, 6 V).
The Voltage column is in volts (V).
The table has a row where current is 2 A and voltage is 4 V.
The equation multiplies I by R; it does not divide.
At 00:48 the lecturer points at the straight line on the voltage-current graph and says the resistance stays constant.
The transcript says the resistance stays constant, but it does not establish what the graph's axes show; the axes must come from the figure.
No processed evidence covers 00:10; the explanation must not borrow the 00:48 moment.
The video could not be analysed, so no visual evidence is available for it; playback availability is a separate check.
